newsitem.title: ITALY: Italians protest against planned U.S. execution.
newsitem.headline: Italians protest against planned U.S. execution.

text.p: Italians protested outside the U.S. embassy in Rome on Thursday against plans by the state of Virginia to go ahead next week with the execution of a death row prisoner who says he has evidence of his innocence.

About 50 demonstrators joined the protest to call for a halt to the execution of Joseph O'Dell, staged by rights groups Amnesty International, the anti-death penalty organisation Hands Off Cain and the Italian political party La Rete.
Luciano Neri, a La Rete Senator, said O'Dell's fate would be debated in Italy's upper house on Monday.
"We are sure the whole parliament will agree to ask the American government and the state governor of Virginia to stop the death penalty in this case against an innocent man," Neri told Reuters.
O'Dell, 55, was convicted in 1985 of the murder of 44-year-old secretary Helen Schartner and sentenced to death.
DNA testing subsequently showed that blood found on his shirt did not match that of the victim, according to published reports.
Supporters say a court of appeals refused to admit the evidence and review the case because a submission deadline had expired. The execution is scheduled for December 18.
Italy has no death penalty in civilian criminal cases and is among the most vociferous supporters of calls for the worldwide abolition of capital punishment.
O'Dell's fate has also stirred the Vatican.
Its semi-official newspaper L'Osservatore Romano on Wednesday criticised what it called a legalistic approach to the case and urged a review.
